label: Delimiter / late original-phase token after several early-group letters (b,d,f,h,i,o,p,r,a,m,u,0) were seen
explanation: Fires almost only during the original phase and at the <DEL> step; it is essentially silent during copy (0.4% of mass) and never at t=0. About 65% of the mass is at the <DEL> step, but only 37% of delimiter steps fire. The rest is late original-phase steps: the rate rises with t and with L, and 95% of the mass is on first occurrences of a token. Whether it fires depends on token content. It needs an accumulated history of group-A tokens (b,d,f,h,i,o,p,r, and more weakly a,m,u,0), with the strongest effect when these come first in the sequence (first_tok d/o/i/f/r/b/p gives about a 2x lift). It fires when the current input is <DEL> or a group-B token (t,c,1,n,z,s,w,l). Inputs k, v, y and 2 rarely fire. The neuron seems to be a graded, roughly additive accumulator over token identities rather than a crisp boolean, so a count threshold only partly captures it. Top activations come at <DEL> or at the last B tokens of length-8/9 sequences whose early tokens are mostly group A. Magnitude was checked only through quartile coverage, which rises with activation.
